name: Yaroame
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.source_named: Perri Ferreira 2017, 'Caracterizacao fonologica do yaroame do Ajarani e Serra do Pacu'; Perri Ferreira, 'Esboco gramatical do Yaroame' (not found online)

sources.citation: Ferreira, Helder Perri. 2017. Yanomama Clause Structure. PhD dissertation, Radboud University Nijmegen (LOT 475), part 1. Ch. 1 §1.4 pp. 10-12, p. 25; ch. 2 p. 38; §2.5 pp. 52ff.
sources.note: Describes Yanomam of Papiu (yano1262), not Yaroamë. On Yaroamë it says only (p. 38): 'The remaining languages of the family – Ninam (Gomez-Goodwin, 1990) and Yãroamë (Perri Ferreira, 2011) – have only six contrastive vowels'; and (p. 25) that the author 'wrote the first grammatical description (also a sketch) on Ỹaroamë' in 2011. §2.5 stress (penultimate, non-contrastive, enclitic exceptions) is stated for YMA only.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2015. Change request 2015-021 (create yro Yaroamë), adopted 2016-01-15; new-code form 2015-021_yro.
sources.note: Bibliographic only; sole published source cited is Ferreira 2011, Esboço gramatical do Ỹaroamë (Rio de Janeiro: Museu do Índio).

sources.citation: Prodoclin (Museu do Índio) Ninam/Yãroamɨ project pages: /etnias/ninam, /lingua, /projeto, /povo, /produtos-e-pesquisa, /etnias/yawari; ISA acervo povo 'Yanomami Ỹaroamë'; PIB Yanomami; Biblioteca Digital Curt Nimuendajú search; Hutukara site search; en/pt Wikipedia
sources.note: Catalogue probes; none hosts a Yaroamë grammar, phonology or profile. Prodoclin hosts only Ninam reports (fetched sources above).

sources.citation: Ferreira, Helder Perri; Machado, Ana Maria Antunes; Senra, Estêvão Benfica (orgs.). 2019. As línguas Yanomami no Brasil: diversidade e vitalidade. São Paulo: ISA / IPHAN. 115 pp. (§1.4.4 Língua Ỹaroamë pp. 50-55; ch. 3 comparative phonology pp. 60-63)
sources.note: Nothing on Yaroamë stress. The Ỹaroamë section (p. 51) only notes the language has /x/, /ʃ/ and /h/ (a source of unintelligibility for other Yanomami) and six short vowels; the comparative-phonology chapter (pp. 60-63) covers consonant correspondences and syllable structure and its only prosodic remark is that Ninam coda consonants come from 'elisão do núcleo vocálico da sílaba póstônica da palavra em Proto-Yanomami' (p. 62). p. 55 box: the 2011 sketch was 'Disponível em www.linguasyanomami.org/grm_yrm/' (domain now NXDOMAIN; no Wayback/arquivo.pt/Common Crawl capture found).

sources.citation: Ferreira, Helder Perri & Goodwin Gómez, Gale. 2012. Perfil (tipológico) da Língua Ninam. PRODOCLIN/Museu do Índio site text (set. 2012). 22 pp.
sources.note: Describes Ninam (sister language), not Yaroamë; contains no stress statement at all (grep acento/tônica = 0). Mentions Yaroamɨ only as 'outra língua menor... sendo documentada'.

sources.citation: Ferreira, Helder Perri. 2012. Relatório Final de Atividades (etapa II, abril/2011-março/2012), Projeto de Documentação das Línguas Ninam e Ỹaroamë, PRODOCLIN / Museu do Índio. 35 pp.
sources.note: Silent on stress. §2.3.1.2 (Ỹaroamë orthography workshop) describes 6 short vowels, [ɨ] as nasal allophone of /ə/ (ỹaroamë = /ɲaɾoamə/ [ɲãɾoamɨ]), and the /x/ vs /h/ contrast; Table 6 lists the delivered products 'esboço gramatical', 'proposta de ortografia', 'cartilha de alfabetização' for yãroamë – Serra do Pacu (not hosted online).

sources.citation: Ferreira, Helder Perri. 2010. Bibliografia comentada. Projeto de Documentação das línguas ninam e yaroamɨ, PRODOCLIN. 18 pp.
sources.note: Annotated bibliography only; records that Ramirez 1994 was the first to present yaroamɨ as an independent language; no linguistic description.

sources.citation: Migliazza, Ernest Cesar. 1972. Yanomama Grammar and Intelligibility. PhD dissertation, Indiana University. 472 pp.
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: online with a Harvard login (also: harvard online access (harvardkey))
sources.note: No Yaroamë data: Language A = Yanam (Ninam) of the Mucajaí/Uraricaá; 'Jawari' of the Ajarani is mentioned only as an ethnonym (pp. 22, 384). Stress rules given are for Yanam/Yanomam/Yanomamɨ/Sanɨma, not for the Ajarani/Serra do Pacu variety.

sources.citation: Fabre, Alain. Diccionario etnolingüístico y guía bibliográfica de los pueblos indígenas sudamericanos: Yanomami (online PDF, 18 pp.)
sources.note: Bibliographic guide; no Yaroamë-specific entry, no description.

sources.citation: Ferreira, Helder Perri. 2011. Esboço gramatical do Ỹaroamë: Língua Yanomami falada do Serra do Pacu/RR. Rio de Janeiro: Museu do Índio / PRODOCLIN. 75 pp.

sources.access_detail: open link recorded by Glottolog or the catalog, not checked; access check: not located online or at Harvard
sources.note: The first and only grammatical description of Yaroamë (Serra do Pacu dialect); a 75-page sketch with a phonology chapter is the most likely home of a stress statement. The 2019 ISA book (p. 55) says it was available at www.linguasyanomami.org/grm_yrm/, but that domain no longer resolves (NXDOMAIN 2026-09-17) and no web-archive capture was found; Glottolog/hh holds a copy. Ask Museu do Índio (Prodoclin), the author, or Hammarström.

sources.citation: Ramirez, Henri. 1994. Le parler yanomamɨ des Xamatauteri. Thèse de doctorat, Université de Provence (Aix-Marseille I).
